headline: Approved minivan and equipment bids and amended policies on home study students and student expression.
summary: The superintendent discussed a federal search warrant served on former leader Stephanie Phillips over alleged embezzlement; no charges have been filed. The board also discussed FY28 budget assumptions and strategic plan development.
decisions: Approved the consent agenda, including bids for maintenance equipment and minivans, by unanimous vote.
Approved a finding that the superintendent is in partial compliance with Policy Title 2.2, by unanimous vote.
Amended policies C6 on home study students and C11 on student freedom of expression, by unanimous vote.

6. Chair's Report 
   
6.1 Merger Study Committee 
We will hold space at our monthly board meetings to review and discuss the work of this 
merger study committee. We are off to a strong foundational start with the creation of our 
own study committee website. This will afford all three districts and their communities 
(Burlington, South Burlington and Winooski) the ability to access and review all 
committee activity and updates as well as warn all of our public meetings.     
6.2 Staff/Student Recognition 
Simon Parlante - Outstanding Community Partner with Vermont Youth Conservation 
Corps (VYCC).  At this time I would like to begin by recognizing Simon Parlante for his 
recognition as an Outstanding Community Partner from the Vermont Youth Conservation 
Corps (VYCC).    
Simon is the Employment Training Specialist at Burlington High School. Our 
Communications Specialist, Russ Elek, wants you to know that in addition to his work 
Page 2 of 7
Draft
with BHS students, Simon is also a coach for his son’s cross county team at South 
Burlington Middle School, who won the State Championship this year. While that deserves 
kudos, we are going to let South Burlington’s superintendent congratulate him on that.  
We are here today because of Simon’s summer work with BHS students. Over the past two 
summers, Burlington High School students have continued to build meaningful 
connections with the Vermont Youth Conservation Corps, gaining hands-on work 
experience while contributing to the Vermont community. Approximately 22 BHS 
students have participated in VYCC programs.  
Through the VYCC Farm Crew, students have gained practical experience in sustainable 
agriculture while developing skills that translate directly to the workplace, including 
teamwork, communication, problem-solving, and time management. Students have 
participated in preparing beds, planting, weeding, harvesting, processing chickens, and 
other farm tasks. 
This growing partnership was recently recognized by Vermont Youth Conservation Corp, 
which honored Simon as an Outstanding Community Partner for his work connecting BHS 
students with VYCC opportunities. VYCC staff members Chris Humphrey, their Food & 
Farm Program Manager; Bo Malcolm, the Senior Community Business Manager; and 
Christine Hadekel each recognized Simon’s commitment to supporting students and 
strengthening the partnership between VYCC and BHS. They highlighted his willingness to 
go above and beyond to help students access opportunities and have positive 
experiences at VYCC. 
Simon, on behalf of BSD, I want to say congratulations on this recognition and thank you 
for all the ways you impact students not just in Burlington, but around Chittenden County 
as well. Please join me in giving Simon a round of applause.  
Commended Scholars from the National Merit Program:  
Arlo Bolles and Elliott R. Throop 
I am also thrilled to also recognize two outstanding students from our district: Arlo Bolles 
and Elliott R. Throop. They are both 12th-grade students at BHS and have been 
recognized as National Merit Commended Scholars. 
The National Merit Scholarship Program is a prestigious national academic competition 
that has been recognizing exceptional high school students since 1955. Each year, more 
than 1.2 million students across the country enter the program by taking the PSAT. 
Out of all the students nationwide who take this exam, only two to three percent score 
high enough to earn Commended Student status. This year, both Arlo and Elliott achieved 
this incredible honor, placing their scores among the top two to three percent of all test-
takers in the nation. This is a clear testament to their hard work, dedication, and 
academic excellence, as well as the educators who have helped them along the way.  
Beyond their achievements in the classroom, Arlo and Elliott are well-rounded students 
who contribute to our school community in many ways, including as key members of our 
music programs for all four years. Arlo is the senior soloist in Violin at the Vermont Youth 
Orchestra, and Elliot plays multiple instruments, including the French Horn. We are truly 
lucky to have Arli and Elliot in BSD. 
Please join me in congratulating Arlo and Elliott on this amazing achievement!

7. Superintendent's Report  
7.1 Discussion: October Superintendent Reflection 
Stephanie Phillips 
Tonight, I also want to address an issue that is on all of our minds and has been deeply 
challenging for our entire district. As was made public last week, a search warrant was 
issued for Stephanie Phillips, a former and longtime leader in BSD, regarding alleged 
embezzlement. 
Before sharing details, I want to emphasize that these are allegations. In our legal system, 
every individual is presumed innocent until proven guilty in a court of law. At the same 
time, I want to speak directly to this situation, balancing our commitment to full 
responsibility and oversight with acknowledging the profound strain this investigation 
places on our community's trust. 
Stephanie served in a role that oversaw a significant budget. Because she was intimately 
familiar with our internal controls, she was positioned to navigate around our systems of 
checks and balances. It is important for the public and the Board to understand how these 
alleged actions went undetected for so long. 
First, BSD conducts an independent annual audit, and those external auditors did not flag 
these discrepancies. As our legal team noted, even the strongest financial controls 
ultimately rely on individuals to oversee them, and if someone in a position of trust is 
determined to bypass systems, they can find ways to do so. 
Second, regarding the pattern of invoices, over a multi-year period across multiple district 
administrations, business office staff, and department leaders, it is alleged that invoices 
were submitted from a company for items closely aligned with our core educational 
priorities. Because individual invoices were kept under the monetary threshold that 
requires Superintendent and Board approval, and because the descriptions matched our 
core work, they did not trigger flags within the Business Office. 
It was only when Stephanie left the district this Spring and new leadership stepped into 
her former office that possible discrepancies were uncovered. Specifically, we learned 
that payments were being made to a company that did not appear to be delivering actual 
products or value to BSD. 
As soon as we uncovered this concern, we acted immediately. In June, the moment I 
learned about the possible discrepancies, I investigated, verified the concern, and notified 
the Burlington Police Department. I also promptly notified our Board Leadership and the 
Vermont Agency of Education. 
BPD brought in the FBI. To protect the integrity of their investigation, federal authorities 
requested that we keep the circle of knowledge strictly limited. My team and I assisted 
federal agents closely throughout their work. 
While no arrest has been made and no formal charges have been filed, federal law 
enforcement served a search warrant on Ms. Phillips and her property last week. Agents 
searched her home, electronic devices, and records related to an alleged shell company, 
Leading and Learning VT. The U.S. Attorney has not named any other family members or 
BSD employees. 
The U.S. Attorney has informed us not to expect any possible indictment before 
Page 4 of 7
Draft
Thanksgiving. In complex financial investigations, federal prosecutors require time to 
thoroughly review all seized materials. Legal counsel has also noted that prosecutors 
sometimes use this period to review evidence or negotiate plea agreements. 
While we navigate this difficult news and respect the legal presumption of innocence, we 
accept full responsibility for evaluating our systems and ensuring our district is protected 
moving forward. We are currently developing an independent financial review to 
thoroughly evaluate our financial controls, identify systemic vulnerabilities, and 
implement safeguards. In the meantime, we have updated our procurement practices and 
procedures to tighten our controls.  
This situation has dealt a heavy blow to our community’s trust and to the dedicated 
educators and staff who work tirelessly every day for our students. If the allegations are 
true, our students, staff, and community have become victims of a crime committed by 
someone who was in a trusted leadership position. We are doing our best to be honest 
and transparent about this. We are also taking a restorative approach to this within the 
district, offering space for our staff to come together to process this news.  
We remain fully committed to cooperating with federal authorities, protecting public 
funds and seeking the return of our funds, and keeping this Board and our community 
updated to the extent we are able as the legal process moves forward. 
In addition to this news about Stephanie, there is a lot of positive work happening in our 
schools. October is always a busy month, and this was no different. We conducted 
Literacy and Math Screeners, which are quick tests done to see where students are and 
what they need. We identified students who need academic support to set up intervention 
groups for them. We also solidified our educator teams, called Professional Learning 
Communities (PLC), who are focused on student learning. And we held parent/teacher 
conferences and professional learning for staff.  
We are also excited to announce that we were awarded a 500k Nellie Mae Grant for 
District-Community Partnership. 
Victor Prussack, Maria Davies, Katherine Grykien and Sparks led these efforts for the 
district, developing a Community Design Team who applied for the grant and focused on 
4 areas – community engagement and partnership, peer tutoring in neighborhood-based 
academic hubs, and English classes for staff. More details to come, but I wanted you to 
know. 
And last but not least, voting is happening at 4 of our schools today and has been going 
well. At BHS it was another way for our community to see and be a part of the new 
building.
